title: 〜っぽい
simpleExplanation: Attaches to nouns, い-adjective stems and a few ます-stems, and conjugates as an い-adjective. 子供っぽい (childish) is critical, unlike 子供らしい (charmingly childlike).
whenUsed: Casual description of appearance, colour or a tendency.
formation: N + っぽい (子供っぽい, 水っぽい)
い-adj stem + っぽい (安っぽい, 白っぽい)
V-ます stem + っぽい (忘れっぽい, 怒りっぽい)

similarGrammar.difference: Typical of, in a good way: 男らしい (manly). っぽい can be critical.
Tends to (actions, undesirable): 遅刻しがち. っぽい is about qualities and appearance.

commonMistakes.why: らしい is positive ("a proper child"); for a criticism use っぽい.
Verbs attach with the ます stem.
い-adjectives drop い before っぽい.

usageNotes: 子供っぽい (childish, negative) vs 子供らしい (childlike, appropriate). Common: 怒りっぽい, 飽きっぽい, 安っぽい, 水っぽい, 男っぽい.
In slang, っぽい after a clause means "seems like": 雨っぽい, 行くっぽい (very casual).
jlptTips: A description with a hint of criticism (acting like, looking cheap, tending to) = っぽい.
The らしい / っぽい contrast is a common item: positive typicality = らしい, negative imitation = っぽい.
Check the stem: ます stem for verbs, adjective stem without い.
